page: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, featuring 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, alongside a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. This instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance paired with weaker multi-core and memory capabilities. The single-core stress-ng score of 2072.67 and Geekbench single-core score of 1673.0 both rank in the average tier. Single-threaded gzip compression performs strongly at 33.01 GB/sec. However, multi-core execution is limited, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 4121.76 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3059.0, both falling into the weak category. Memory performance is also constrained, as evidenced by a poor Passmark memory score of 1168.36 and a weak large-block write bandwidth of 21.07 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D2pds_v6 offers a low-cost entry point into ARM-based cloud computing with dedicated physical cores and integrated local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-threaded and memory-intensive performance relative to x86 alternatives. This server is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded file compression tasks, and development or testing environments that benefit from local SSD storage without requiring high memory bandwidth or dense multi-core processing.
